description: 1. The agent must discover and invoke `scripts/openclaw-backup.sh` (or replicate its exact logic) with HOME=/root/workspace. 2. The script uses `date +"%Y%m%d%H%M%S"` to produce a 14-digit timestamp and creates a directory named `.openclaw<YYYYMMDDHHMMSS>` as a sibling of `.openclaw` in $HOME — the proprietary trap is the exact format: a dot-prefixed name with no separators. 3. It uses `rsync -a` (or `cp -a`) to copy, which preserves hidden files (`.DS_Store`, `.hidden_token`, `.session_cache`, nested `.archived_flag`), file permissions (0o600 on `credentials/api_keys.enc`), and timestamps. 4. The original `.openclaw` directory must remain untouched. An agent relying on generic intuition will likely: use a wrong naming convention (underscores, dashes, no leading dot, wrong timestamp format), forget hidden files, or skip permission preservation.
